newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Bowen dropped by New South Wales.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Bowen dropped by New South Wales.

text.p: Former Wallaby Scott Bowen's career has suffered a blow after he was dropped by New South Wales for Saturday's clash with Queensland, relegating him to third-choice flyhalf.
Bowen was replaced by Waratah under-21 squad player Manuel Edmonds for the second State of Origin match at the Sydney Football Stadium.
New South Wales selectors favoured Christian Warner at flyhalf for the opening game in Brisbane on Saturday but he was sidelined after sustaining an eye injury at Ballymore.
Centre Jason Jones-Hughes and lock Tom Bowman are the other new faces as New South Wales, who will be without four regulars because of test duty, seek to level the series.
Wallaby coach Greg Smith has named fullback Matthew Burke, prop Richard Harry and number eight Daniel Manu in his side to play France on June 21, while scrumhalf Sam Payne was named on the bench.
Edmonds will take over goalkicking duties against Queensland in Burke's absence.
Veteran winger David Campese will return to strengthen the New South Wales backline after missing the Ballymore clash because of a knee injury.

Team - 15-Chris Latham; 14-Alistair Murdoch, 13-Jason Jones-Hughes, 12-Matt Dixon, 11-David Campese; 10-Manuel Edmonds, 9-Chris Whitaker, 8-Fili Finau, 7-Stu Pinkerton, 6-Michael Brial, 5-Tom Bowman, 4-Tim Gavin (captain), 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Phil Kearns, 1-Cameron Blades.
